title: The leak words measured on real columns before a change: they stay
request: The owner: fix the false leak alarms (contract_duration, post_code) with a small, measured change to the name rule.
spec: decide.rule's feature.leakage_suspect flags a column whose name has a leak word; the notebook reviews ask it from the name alone since 22.8's follow-up.
plan: Measure the rule on labelled leak decisions
Measure it on every real column name
Change the words only if the measurement says so
Pin the measurement as a test

decisions.decision: The leak words are not changed
decisions.why: on the real columns every flag is a known leak and the word duration makes four of the six catches; the two harmless names came from a demo notebook and a reviewer's example, not from real data

decisions.decision: The invented decision sets are not used to judge the change
decisions.why: their generator never writes names like post_code or contract_duration, so they cannot show the false alarm at all
a later change to the leak words must keep every real flag a known leak and every name-visible real leak caught

change: tests/test_name_rule_real_columns.py (column names of the committed real datasets only, never a row).

findings.defect: The planned fix would have removed true leak catches
findings.scenario: Dropping duration from the leak words to quiet contract_duration.
findings.cause: duration is the word that catches bank marketing's call duration and online shoppers' three page-duration columns, all measured leaks.
findings.fix: No change to the words; the false alarm stays visible for a person to answer, which becomes a label.

measurements.name: name rule on real column names
measurements.gate: every flagged real column is a known leak, decided before the change
measurements.result: 269 names in 12 datasets: 6 flagged, 6 known leaks, 0 harmless; 4 of the 6 caught by duration

measurements.name: name rule on invented labelled decisions (dev and train, never sealed)
measurements.gate: false alarms by word, to see whether post or duration cause any
measurements.result: 4 false alarms in about 6,500 decisions, all from refund in prior_refund_count; none from post or duration

outcome: The leak words stay as they are, now pinned by a test on real column names.
lessons: Measure a proposed fix on the data where the problem would show; a set made by a generator that never writes the name cannot judge it.
A false alarm seen once in a demo is weaker evidence than four true catches in real tables.
risks: Only 12 real datasets: a harmless real name with a leak word may still exist elsewhere; the person's answer is the way to learn it.
